summary: Short-lived 5xx surge during route weight convergence causing upstream runtime restarts for SparkDocs
description: At ~18:12 UTC on 2026-03-14 SparkDocs observed a sudden uptick in 5xx responses from the Redwood API for ~12 minutes. Error rate climbed from baseline ~0.6% to a peak ~48% for the customer's tenant traffic. Customers reported failed short-generation calls and broken streaming sessions. The spike coincided with a weight rebalance event that shifted a portion of traffic to a model variant that triggered repeated upstream runtime restarts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer traffic pattern: high concurrency burst of short token requests to embeddings and chat endpoints. 2) Weighted-route rebalance triggered by autoscaler after tenant capacity change. 3) Traffic shifted to a variant with an updated kernel selection profile (quantized path). 4) Upstream runtime processes logged GPU driver resets and terminated, causing API gateway to return 502/503 for inflight requests. Reproduced in staging by simulating a tenant scale-up while flipping route weights to the new variant.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: routing weight shift exposed a model variant that hits a rarely exercised kernel path leading to GPU driver instability. Evidence: concurrent nvml GPU reset messages on multiple runtimes that received the traffic, timestamps align with weight-change event in routing logs. Additional contributing factor: autoscaler triggered node recycle at same time, increasing the chance of kernel selection/driver reinitialization race. We reproduced a fail-case in staging by forcing a variant flip + simulated kernel swap; observed identical nvml reset and segfault. Mitigation sequence applied in prod prevented further restarts.

2026-03-15T09:12:00Z - Eng (Liam Chen): Deployed hotfix to runtime (github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4312) and updated routing PR to debounce weight convergence (github.com/redwood/routing/pull/218). Monitoring in prod shows steady error rate back to baseline.
resolution: Root cause: concurrent route weight convergence and autoscaler-driven node recycling exposed a kernel-selection edge-case in the quantized execution path, provoking NVML GPU resets and upstream runtime crash loops. Immediate mitigation: rolled back weights to stable variant, sequentially restarted affected runtimes to break crash loops, and applied temporary guard to routing to prevent abrupt weight swaps. Permanent fixes: runtime patch to handle GPU resets without crashing, and routing change to debounce weight convergence and add a graceful warmup handshake for kernel swaps.
